title: Find Median from Data Stream
pattern: Two heaps: smaller half and larger half
statement: Design a class that receives numbers one at a time (`addNum`) and can report the **median** of everything received so far (`findMedian`). With an even count, the median is the average of the two middle numbers.

example.input:
MedianFinder()
addNum(5)
addNum(2)
findMedian()  →  3.5
addNum(8)
findMedian()  →  5
addNum(1)
findMedian()  →  3.5
example.why: After 5, 2: median (2 + 5) / 2 = 3.5. After 8: the middle of 2, 5, 8 is 5. After 1: (2 + 5) / 2 = 3.5.

more.input:
MedianFinder()
addNum(1)
addNum(2)
findMedian()  →  1.5
addNum(3)
findMedian()  →  2

idea: Re-sorting after every insertion is too slow. But the median only depends on the **middle** of the sorted order.

Split the numbers into a smaller half and a larger half. Keep the smaller half in a max-heap (its largest on top) and the larger half in a min-heap (its smallest on top). The middle values are then always at the two tops.
After every insertion, rebalance so the halves differ in size by at most one (the smaller half may hold the extra number). The median is that extra top, or the average of both tops.

complexity.time: O(log n) per add, O(1) per median
complexity.timeWhy: Adding does a constant number of heap pushes and pops; the median just reads the tops.
complexity.spaceWhy: Every number is stored in one of the two heaps.
